newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares hold at new highs, dollar steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares hold at new highs, dollar steady.

text.p: Share prices in London and Frankfurt hit new highs again on Monday morning with investors encouraged by Friday's record-breaking trading sessions around the world, though the momentum of the gains slowed.
Meanhwile, The dollar was steady, off overnight levels but still keeping well within its recent ranges.
Dealers attributed the European gains to Friday's 60-point rise on Wall Street which carried it to a new closing high of 5,992.86 following weaker than expected U.S. jobs data.

Investors worldwide celebrated the data, believing it would deter the U.S. Federal Reserve from a long-feared tightening of monetary policy. London and Frankfurt also closed at record highs on Friday.

In London, Europe's largest bourse, shares were slightly higher in late-morning trade, but some way off the new highs set earlier in the day on the back of Wall Street's record run. The market was sustained by heavy interest in selected stocks.
The FTSE 100 share index stood at 4,033.7 by 1100 GMT, up 8.9 points on the day, after touching a new record high of 4046.8 points in earlier trade.
"The market was squeezed tightly on Wall Street," one marketmaker said.
But others were more cautious, saying investors were becoming increasingly nervous of the market's heady altitude.
Some also said the FTSE index's strength also masked what they called a "patchy" rally, characterised by stockpicking.
"I'm concerned by the relative narrowness of this rally...Unless it broadens out we would have to question the FTSE's ability to hold all its gains," one dealer said.

British Airways was one of the shares in favour, touching a new high of 617p before settling back to trade 11p higher at 605-1/2p. The stock gained heavily on Friday on hopes airlines will in future be able to trade take-off and landing slots more openly.

Investors also homed in on oil stocks after a report in the Wall Street Journal that Shell Oil and Texaco were in talks to merge their U.S. refining and marketing businesses. Shell shares were up 14-1/2p at 1,013-1/2p while British Petroleum was up 11p at 698-1/2.
Dealers said the market showed little reaction to a surprise drop in British industrial output in August.

German shares were also higher at midday with the DAX index breaking through to a new high just above 2700 points, a gain of around 0.64 percent, after the DAX Ibis closed above 2700 on Friday in post-exchange trading.

French shares were showing small gains at midday after spending most of the morning in negative territory as the bourse continued its consolidation. Brokers said the market was technically well oriented, but was still digesting the market's recent climb to the 2,150 level.

In currencies, the dollar retreated from tough resistance at 112 yen overnight, partly due to comments from senior officials of two of Japan's political parties calling for an increase in interest rates after the general election set for October 20.
But dealers said the impact from the comments was slight and seen more as an effort to generate votes from savers rather than a shift in monetary policy.

A senior official of Japan's Liberal Democratic Party, the biggest member of the country's ruling coalition, was quoted by a news agency earlier saying a rise in the official discount rate will probably be considered after the election.
Separately, Ichiro Ozawa, head of the main opposition party Shinshinto, also said Japan's interest rate levels must be corrected. He said the unfavourable effects of low rates were spreading.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was at 111.45 yen and 1.5311 marks versus Friday's late European levels of 111.55 yen and 1.5304 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 8.9 points higher at 4,033.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 1.55 points higher at 2,154.24.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt opened 17.33 higher at 2,700.66.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1100 GMT
Gold fixed at $379.60 after closing at $380.45 an ounce on Friday. Silver was weaker at $4.87, off four cents.
